title: React Native: Screen and controls
lead: Use the iOS or Android development build to change a source, compare Player UI, inspect applied settings and try SDK operations. The steps below follow the screen from playback and configuration to command results and events.

blocks.text: Open Player Lab React Native on iOS or Android. The top of the screen contains the UI choices, native video and source buttons. Playback helpers, the state line, Show API experiments and Show configuration follow below. VOD means on-demand media with a fixed timeline; a live source may also provide a rewind window, labeled DVR in this app.

blocks.title: Before opening the screen
blocks.text: Use the generated Expo development build; Expo Go does not include these native Player modules. The iOS bundle identifier and Android package are both com.playerlab.reactnative. The Player license must allow that identifier on the platform being used. Follow the linked setup and repository instructions to generate the host or refresh its copied local configuration.

items.label: Generate and run the Expo development host
Implementation guide: integration, configuration and UI changes

blocks.text: Choose a source and apply a change

blocks.caption: The iOS configuration form shows source type, title, poster, external subtitle fields and the initial-position reference. The local URL in this capture is an example from that test environment.
The Android form includes the same external WebVTT inputs. Enter a URL reachable from the device; the address shown in a capture is not a preset to copy unchanged.

items: Choose a VOD source button and start playback in the Player UI. iOS offers HLS and progressive MP4 in the form and hides DASH presets; Android also offers DASH. HLS and DASH are streaming formats that can provide several qualities.

Open Show configuration. Record the current source and Player values before editing. The source URL must use HTTP or HTTPS; match Source type to the actual media. Title, poster URL and start offset are optional.

For a visible first change, keep the source URL, enter 5 in Start offset (seconds), choose Start and select Apply and recreate player. If Autoplay is off, start playback in the Player UI. Check the new SourceLoaded log entry and the starting position.

After a successful Apply, inspect Show applied code and the actual picture. Apply validates the complete draft and recreates the Player even for a source-only form change. Invalid or unchanged settings leave the current Player in place.

Use Reset draft to discard edits that have not been applied. To undo an applied change, restore the recorded values and Apply again. A source preset restores source fields immediately while retaining Player settings; it is not a reset of every option.

rows: Apply recreates the Player. Compare whether the new session starts automatically and starts muted. These switches describe startup behavior, not an immediate play or mute command.
Compare the initial position after Apply. Start refers to the beginning of the media or live rewind window; End refers to the end or live edge. SDK default is Start for VOD and End for live.
Compare bufferConfig.audioAndVideo.forwardDuration in applied code. This is a media buffer target, not a guaranteed startup delay. Blank restores the platform default.
Compare adaptationConfig.maxSelectableBitrate and the selected quality on a source with several qualities. Enter bits per second without units or commas; blank removes the cap.

blocks.text: Offsets and buffer durations accept finite decimal seconds. The buffer field permits zero for automatic selection on iOS; Android requires a positive value or blank. Maximum bitrate accepts whole numbers up to the native/JavaScript integer limit, explained in the implementation guide. Initial Player values are Autoplay off, Mute on startup off, and blank buffer/bitrate. Allow DVR controls the app’s rewind helper rather than an SDK creation property.
Compare playback, tracks and Player UI

blocks.caption: The iOS build after selecting an external subtitle in the Player menu. A timed cue is visible over the native video.
The Android build with the selected external subtitle displayed. The subtitle is enabled through the Player’s track selection, not by Mark as default alone.

items: Use the Player’s play/pause and seek controls to check the selected source. On a live source with a rewind window, compare Live edge and the rewind buttons; the state line reports availability and distance behind live. A VOD source cannot demonstrate a live rewind window.

Choose Default, Sports, Live (DVR) or Cinema in the UI row. The change recreates the Player and reloads the applied source. Compare the rendered controls and then the UI values in Show applied code. Keep the same source to compare presentation.

To add a subtitle, open Show configuration and enter External WebVTT URL, Subtitle label and Subtitle language together. WebVTT is a text file containing timed subtitle cues; use one aligned with the selected media. A language tag such as en-US identifies the language.

Apply, then choose the label in the Player subtitle menu and play through a cue. Mark as default supplies track metadata and does not enable the track by itself. If the source has alternate audio, compare its available audio tracks in the Player menu.

To remove the external track, clear External WebVTT URL and Apply; the associated label/language values are cleared as well. Selecting a source preset restores its source fields. To undo a UI comparison, select the previous UI; restore other applied Player values separately.

blocks.title: Scrolling inside the Android Player menu
blocks.text: The video menu and the surrounding form scroll separately. Start the swipe inside the video menu to reach its lower items, or outside the video to scroll the form. The app keeps an active player gesture with the video so the parent ScrollView does not take that drag.

items.label: UI customization, platform differences and FAQ

blocks.caption: Show applied code in the iOS build, with Apply/Reset controls, Copy code and the license placeholder. The output excludes pending draft edits.

items: Open Show applied code after Apply. Read the Player, source and selected UI settings together. Record the output before changing another value so the difference is clear.

Edit a draft value without applying it: the displayed applied configuration stays unchanged. Reset draft cancels that edit. Apply commits a valid changed draft and updates the output after recreating the Player.

Use Copy code when you need the applied settings outside the screen. This uses Expo Clipboard in the native development build. The output uses license placeholders; retain those placeholders when sharing an example.
For how the settings connect to usePlayer, PlayerView and the shared UI files, follow the implementation guide. The displayed configuration is not an export of every internal SDK default.

items.label: How the current code applies settings

blocks.text: Edit additional SDK settings and lists

An SDK is the library used to integrate the Player. Its API exposes configuration, commands and events. The basic form provides common options; Additional SDK configuration and the list editors expose further properties from the installed React Native wrapper. A native SDK feature absent from the wrapper cannot be enabled by inventing an extra key.

items: In Show configuration, find Additional SDK configuration. Search an exact path such as SourceConfig.description and select Set this API value. Keep the original value or whether the override was absent.
Enter a value using the displayed type. A list accepts one item per line; a map accepts unique name=value entries; SDK enumerations provide their declared choices. This changes the draft until Apply.

For arrays, open Subtitle lists and advertising, select the source or offline subtitle list and use Edit this list and Add list item. Complete each track’s URL, label, language and format. SourceConfig.subtitleTracks and OfflineContentConfig.sourceConfig.subtitleTracks are separate lists.

Apply and recreate player, inspect Show applied code and compare the relevant playback/menu/event result. Advanced overrides take priority over the basic form. Remove an override and Apply to restore its form value or SDK default; an enabled empty list explicitly clears that array.

blocks.text: Advertising list items need a position and one or more ad sources. A schedule is input to the SDK, not confirmation that an ad tag, service or media is available. Offline operations likewise need downloadable content, storage and any required DRM rights; use a stable content identifier. The implementation guide explains the corresponding configuration objects.
Try callbacks and native UI handlers

blocks.caption: The iOS callbacks editor shows the selected network callback, its signature and an explicitly enabled body. This captured example changes volume and returns the request.

items: Under JavaScript callbacks and native UI handlers, search PlayerConfig.networkConfig.preprocessHttpRequest and select Edit this callback. Read the arguments and required return type before editing.

Enter a function body, enable Allow edited JavaScript execution and Apply. The supplied default returns the request; the callback runs when a matching SDK request occurs. Inspect the event log and any deliberate visible effect.

Network callbacks may return a Promise; synchronous callbacks must return synchronously. Fullscreen and custom-message entries create handler objects rather than plain values. Use the signature and factory requirements shown in the editor.

To stop the experiment, remove the callback and Apply again. If the body changed Player state, restore that state or recreate from the applied configuration. Edited JavaScript runs inside the app without a sandbox; only enable code you trust.

blocks.text: Run commands and inspect state and events

blocks.caption: The Android API panel after running Player.getCurrentTime. It shows the submitted call, returned position, recreation action and Player events.

items: Open Show API experiments, search Player.getCurrentTime, choose a time mode and select Run selected API. Read it again while playback advances. Compare the returned position with the picture; the unit is seconds.

Try a state-changing command such as Player.pause, then inspect Player.isPaused and the matching events. Restore playback with Player.play. A call returning no value means it was dispatched; check the resulting state rather than treating that alone as success.

Use Player events to inspect recent SDK payload summaries. Pause event log freezes recording for comparison; resume it to collect new events, and Clear API event log clears the displayed experiment history.

Use Recreate player after API experiments after destroying the Player or to restore its applied configuration. Resources and track identifiers from a previous source/Player must be queried again after replacement.

blocks.caption: The iOS event log shows onTimeChanged payloads during playback. Event recording and API state queries are separate ways to inspect the same session.

blocks.text: Some operations are platform-specific even when they appear in the search. In wrapper 1.29, Player.setVideoQuality and its auto option act only on Android; iOS reports a warning and does not select a quality. For iOS, compare the configured bitrate boundary and observed quality instead. In the Lab subtitle input, blank passes undefined to Player.setSubtitleTrack to disable subtitles.

For an offline experiment, initialize the manager for the chosen content identifier, request options and inspect onOptionsAvailable before downloading. onCompleted reports completion; Player.loadOfflineContent loads that stored asset. Cancellation, deletion and license operations affect the selected identifier. Restore or delete experimental downloads deliberately; Player recreation is not an offline-storage reset.

blocks.caption: The Android Cast startup panel after a full restart: savedOptions and startupOptions agree, nativeInitialized is true and pendingRestart is false. This does not show receiver playback.

items: In Additional SDK configuration, set BitmovinCastManagerOptions.applicationId and messageNamespace as needed. Blank values use the default receiver and namespace. Keep the previous values for restoration.

Select Save Cast options for next launch in Cast startup configuration. This saves the current draft independently of Apply. Fully close and reopen the app; a JavaScript reload or Player recreation does not restart native Cast.

Select Read native Cast startup state. Compare savedOptions, startupOptions, nativeInitialized and pendingRestart. Android reads the native manager’s public getters; iOS reports the options submitted at process launch.

For discovery, connection and receiver playback, use a compatible receiver on the same network. To restore previous options, save those values and fully restart again. Wrapper 1.29’s deprecated BitmovinCastManager.initialize does not apply edited options.
